deep.reconstruction:
This is page '8' of a 1983 sketch, contemporary with Pursuing Stacks, of what Grothendieck later called derivators; here he calls them 'théories homotopiques'. The setting from the surrounding pages: a pair (M,W) consists of a category M and a class W of weak equivalences. It defines, for each small category A, the localization H_W(A) = Hom(A,M)[W_A^{-1}], where W_A is the class of pointwise weak equivalences. Each functor f: A→B gives f^*, and one asks for adjoints f_! and f_*. Subject to Hyp 1-6 (base change, conservativity and so on), this 2-functor H_W is a 'homotopy theory' in his sense.

(1) Presentations of a fixed H. He proposes to get an overview of all pairs (M,W) that give rise to a given homotopy theory H. A morphism (M1,W1)→(M,W) is a functor preserving weak equivalences. It induces a strict morphism of prederivators H_{W1}→H_W that commutes with the f^*. The precise question: given two presentations (M1,W1), (M2,W2) and a given isomorphism H_{W1} ≅ H_{W2}, is there a third (M,W) with a cospan (M1,W1)→(M,W)←(M2,W2) inducing that isomorphism? In modern terms this is the realization or rigidification problem: are equivalences of derivators induced by (zigzags of) homotopical functors or Quillen equivalences, and how does a fixed derivator's space of models look?

(2) Ex. 3. Take M = Cat and W a fundamental localizer (localisateur fondamental), his axiomatic class of weak equivalences of small categories. He records that he has handled the existence of f_! (homotopy left Kan extension) but not yet f_*. The first word is hard to read: 'pensé' or more likely 'prouvé'. Computing f_! in Cat is relatively easy via the Grothendieck construction and comma categories A/b. f_* (cohomological direct image) is the hard part, and he suspects finiteness hypotheses on A and B may be needed.

The next page goes on with Ex. 4: complexes in an abelian category with quasi-isomorphisms, the derived categories of sheaves on A^{op∧}×T, Rf_*, and Lf_! when (f_top)_! is exact. It also lists base-change and localization axioms (Hyp 4-6).
errors: No outright errors. As posed, the existence of a single cospan is too optimistic in general. Known positive answers (Renaudin; via Dugger presentations for combinatorial model categories) give zigzags of Quillen equivalences rather than a single cospan of weak-equivalence-preserving functors. For arbitrary (M,W) with no model structure, an equivalence of derivators need not lift to an equivalence of the underlying ∞-categories, let alone to a cospan.
A W-preserving functor M1→M induces a morphism commuting with f^*, but not automatically with f_! or f_*. Compatibility with the adjoints is an extra condition he does not address here.

The suspicion that finiteness hypotheses on A, B are needed for f_* in Cat_W turned out to be unnecessary. Cisinski showed that for every fundamental localizer the prederivator Cat_W is a derivator, with f_* for all small A, B.

ideas.what: Question of classifying all presentations (M,W) of a given homotopy theory/derivator, and whether an isomorphism H_{W1}≅H_{W2} is induced by a cospan (M1,W1)→(M,W)←(M2,W2)
ideas.modern_name: Realization/rigidity problem for equivalences of derivators; models of a derivator up to zigzags of Quillen equivalences (cf. moduli of models, DK-equivalences of relative categories)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Renaudin (2009, combinatorial model categories embed 2-fully-faithfully in derivators up to Quillen equivalence); Dugger (2001, presentations); Barwick–Kan (relative categories); Muro–Raptis and Schlichting on the failure of derivator/triangulated invariance
ideas.where_published: Related themes of comparing modelizers in Pursuing Stacks (1983) and Les Dérivateurs (1990–91); this specific cospan formulation unsure

ideas.what: For M=Cat and W a fundamental localizer, existence of f_! and (open) f_* for the prederivator A ↦ Hom(A,Cat)[W_A^{-1}]
ideas.modern_name: Cat_W is a derivator for every fundamental localizer W
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cisinski (thesis / Astérisque 308, 2006; 'Images directes cohomologiques', 2003), exposed by Maltsiniotis (Astérisque 301, 2005)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (fundamental localizers / test categories) and Les Dérivateurs; Maltsiniotis' account of Grothendieck's homotopy theory

ideas.what: Description of 'homotopy theory' H as the family H(A)=Hom(A,M)[W_A^{-1}] with f^*, f_!, f_*
ideas.modern_name: Prederivator/derivator associated with a category with weak equivalences
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Les Dérivateurs), independently Heller (homotopy theories, 1988), Franke (1996)

missed.claim: An explicit 1983 formulation of the realization question for derivator equivalences: given two presentations and an isomorphism of their homotopy theories, find a common target presentation inducing it. This is an early date for the question later answered (in zigzag form, combinatorial case) by Renaudin. The exact cospan version for general (M,W) remains a reasonable but largely untreated question.
missed.quote: Pour deux tels, (M_1,W_1),(M_2,W_2), peut-on trouver un troisième (M,W), et (M_1,W_1)→(M,W), (M_2,W_2)→ donnant naissance à l'iso. donné entre H_{W_1} et H_{W_2} ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck in 1983 asked precisely the question of whether derivators detect equivalences of models. This is the issue at the heart of later work (Renaudin; Muro–Raptis on derivator K-theory; the comparison between derivators and ∞-categories). Historically it is mildly notable, mathematically mostly superseded.

missed.claim: Dating evidence: by 1983 Grothendieck had (reportedly) established f_! for Cat localized at a fundamental localizer but not f_*. He suspected finiteness was needed; Cisinski later showed it is not.
missed.quote: J'ai pensé [prouvé?] l'existence des f!, mais non encore celle des f_*. Il est possible qu'il faille pour les unes faire des hypothèses de finitude sur les A, B
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Clarifies the chronology of the 'derivator' axioms and of Cisinski's resolution of Grothendieck's conjecture that Cat_W is a derivator.

deep.surprise_reason: Both themes are known to be Grothendieck's: fundamental localizers giving derivators, and comparing models. The explicit cospan-realization question for equivalences of homotopy theories, dated 1983, is a nice early formulation of a problem later treated by Renaudin and others. It is not a new result, though.
